title: Hourly Visit Charge Corrections — Personal Services Plan Desk Guidance
content:
An hourly charge on a Personal Services Plan for a delivered visit that the visit record shows was billed on more time than the visit supports is corrected by the Resident and Family Services desk whenever it is found within the package's dispute window of its posting date, without waiting for the resident to raise it. Corrections are made one charge at a time, beginning with the most recently posted hourly charge for a delivered visit.

## What the correction is

The correction is posted as one service dispute credit referencing that hourly charge and carrying the billing month of the charge. The credit lowers the amount owed on the personal services account; the plan's hours are not touched.

A charge re-rated for such a correction is corrected on the re-rated figure even where it matches the delivered minutes, the rounding and the surcharge rules that govern hours when they are first drawn and charged; those rules stay in force for every first posting, and the re-rating applies only to working out a correction.

| Element | As posted |
|---|---|
| Entry corrected | The hourly charge for the delivered visit |
| Kind of credit | Service dispute |
| Billing month carried | The billing month of the hourly charge |
| Number of credits per charge corrected | One |

## Basis questions

**Must the resident first complain?** No. The desk corrects such a charge whenever it is found within the dispute window, without waiting for the resident to raise it.

**Where several hourly charges for delivered visits qualify, which comes first?** The most recently posted one; corrections are made one charge at a time.

**Which credit reason does such a correction carry?** Service dispute.

## Invocation: `post_services_visit_credit_5ef485c2`

**Capability.** The tool posts a money credit on a personal services account against one earlier charge entry. One call books one credit entry dated today that references the charge it corrects, carries its reason and billing month, and lowers the amount owed on the plan by the credited amount; the plan's hours are not touched. The resident sees the credit on the next personal services statement.

**How it is invoked.** `post_services_visit_credit_5ef485c2` is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `services_plan_id` | Reference number of the personal services plan whose account is credited, as returned by the personal services plan lookup | Identifier |
| `source_entry_id` | Reference number of the personal services ledger entry being credited, as returned by the personal services ledger lookup | Identifier |
| `credit_reason` | Why the charge is credited | Exactly one of the enum values below |
| `billing_period` | The plan month the credit relates to, the month of the charge being credited | `YYYY-MM` |
| `amount` | The credit in USD | Positive amount to 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent |

Enum values of `credit_reason`:

- `service_dispute` — a charge corrected because the service was not delivered, was delivered short, or was billed twice;
- `billing_error` — a charge posted against the wrong plan or at the wrong rate;
- `residency_end_proration` — the package fee for the days after a residency's end returned.

**Return.** On success, a dictionary rendered as text with `status` set to `credit_posted`, `services_entry_id` (reference number of the new credit entry), `source_entry_id` (the charge entry credited), `amount` (the credit in USD, 2 decimal places), `posting_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, today) and `account_balance` (the plan's amount owed in USD after the credit, 2 decimal places).

*Illustrative call shape (hypothetical values):* a plan reference, the reference of one hourly charge entry, `service_dispute`, `2026-03` and the credit amount return `credit_posted` with the new entry's reference, the posting date and the amount owed after the credit.
